key_insight: Magnetic Barkhausen noise and thermoelectric power both track storage-related changes in flux-cored welding wires, making them promising non-destructive indicators of consumable degradation.
engineering_relevance: These measurements could help welding engineers decide whether stored flux-cored wires remain fit for use before they are deployed in production.
method: Stored rutile flux-cored wires in four environments for 3, 6, and 12 months
Checked visual condition, then measured Seebeck coefficient, bulk magnetic properties, and Magnetic Barkhausen Noise
Compared storage-time trends and correlations between magnetic and thermoelectric indicators
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong correlations between magnetic and thermoelectric parameters, with some exceeding 0.9 and the MBN Amplitude-to-Envelope Ratio vs. SC reaching r = 0.99 in two environments.
watch_item: The approach needs validation beyond the studied wire type and storage conditions before it can be used as a general industrial acceptance test.
paper_title: Feasibility study of using magnetic and thermoelectric methods for the assessment of storage-induced changes in flux-cored welding wires
